AIInteractionResource.description:
One AI run.

No prompt body, no model response and no credential — the columns do not exist. What is here is
enough to answer which run this was, under whose authority, with which model and pinned prompt,
and what came out (BR-PR-08).
AIInteractionResource.title: AIInteractionResource

AnalysisResource.description: What one Level 1 run produced. Identifiers, so a reviewer can go and look.
AnalysisResource.title: AnalysisResource

ApprovalRecordResource.description: Immutable except for the execution outcome, which is written once.
ApprovalRecordResource.title: ApprovalRecordResource

AttachmentTicketResource.description:
The attachment row plus a short-lived URL to write it (ADR-0039).

The upload does not pass through this API. The client PUTs to `upload_url` and then calls the
complete endpoint, at which point the size and checksum are read from the store rather than
believed from the client.
AttachmentTicketResource.title: AttachmentTicketResource

CommitmentUpdate.description: The due date is absent on purpose: moving a deadline is a renegotiation (BR-C-07).
CommitmentUpdate.title: CommitmentUpdate

CurrentPrincipal.description:
The caller, as this organization sees them.

`roles` is here so a client can render navigation that matches what the caller may do. It is
guidance for the interface and nothing more: the backend re-decides every request, so a client
that ignored this and showed every button would be refused rather than obeyed (contract §14).
CurrentPrincipal.title: CurrentPrincipal

DependencyResource.description:
Endpoints as type and id only.

Deliberately no titles. A dependency tells you your work is waiting on `work:5f3a`; what
`work:5f3a` says is a separate question with its own visibility answer (BR-W-18), and folding it
in here would route around that.
DependencyResource.title: DependencyResource

DuePrecision.description:
Conversational dates are rarely exact.

"By Friday" is a week; "end of the month" is a month; "soon" is vague and must never be turned
into a date, because a system that invents precision produces a missed-deadline alert about a
deadline nobody set.
DuePrecision.title: DuePrecision

EventAttachmentResource.description:
An attachment's metadata. Never its bytes, and never its object key.

The key is server-derived (ADR-0039) and publishing it would let a caller reason about the
bucket layout, which is the one thing that must stay uninteresting.
EventAttachmentResource.title: EventAttachmentResource

EvidenceCreate.description:
A citation.

The locator decides which half of the model applies: a text span requires a verbatim `excerpt`
checked against the Event (BR-E-05), an attachment requires a `claim_summary` because a PDF has
no span to quote (BR-E-14). Supplying both, or neither, is refused.
EvidenceCreate.title: EvidenceCreate

ExternalIdentityResource.description:
The external id is returned as stored.

It is the thing being mapped, so a directory that hid it could not be reviewed. Reading is
organization-wide by ADR-0037 for that reason; what is *not* organization-wide is changing it.
ExternalIdentityResource.title: ExternalIdentityResource

MilestoneList.description: Unpaginated. A Project with more milestones than fit on a page has a different problem.
MilestoneList.title: MilestoneList

ParticipantInputModel.description:
Somebody named on an Event.

`person_id` and `external_handle` are both optional and at least one is required (BR-E-12). The
pairing is the point: a meeting has attendees the system can name, and a channel message has a
number it cannot resolve yet, and both are participants.
ParticipantInputModel.title: ParticipantInputModel

Publishing FastAPI's default validation schema while returning problem+json would make the
document a description of a different service — and a generated client would be built against

rule.description: Business rule id, present on rule violations
rule.title: Rule

Problem.title: Problem

ProposalCreate.description:
A reviewable mutation that has not happened.

`tool` and `arguments` are the action: fully resolved, nothing left to infer at execution. The
tool must exist in the Gateway's registry and the arguments must fit it, checked now so that a
Proposal nobody could execute never reaches a reviewer (ADR-0042).
ProposalCreate.title: ProposalCreate

ProposalRevise.description: BR-PR-02. Produces a new Proposal; the original becomes `superseded`.
ProposalRevise.title: ProposalRevise

ToolCallResource.description: One call the runtime made. Denials are recorded and returned like any other.
ToolCallResource.title: ToolCallResource

UnitStatus.description: Departments and teams share a lifecycle: they are archived, never deleted (BR-G-04).
UnitStatus.title: UnitStatus

UnitStatusChange.description: Archiving a department or a team. Neither is ever deleted (BR-G-04).
UnitStatusChange.title: UnitStatusChange

WorkListItem.description:
Identical to the single-item shape.

A narrower list projection would be an optimisation nobody has measured, and the first client to
need a field the list omits would fetch each row individually — which is slower than sending it.
WorkListItem.title: WorkListItem

Recompute the hash, claim the record once, call one registered tool.

No `If-Match`: this is not an edit of the approval but the single use of it. Idempotence comes
from the record itself — the claim is a conditional update, so a retried execute finds the
approval already spent and is refused rather than running the mutation twice.

put.description:
One call, one transaction, whether or not the seat is currently occupied.

`PUT` because the request states the desired end state rather than an operation: this person is
the owner. Which matrix cell that needs — `ASSIGN` for unowned Work, `REASSIGN` when somebody is
being displaced — depends on the current state, and the service decides it. A router that chose
would be a router implementing authorization policy (contract §3).

No `If-Match`: the precondition here is about who owns the Work, which the service reads and
acts on inside one transaction, not about a version the caller read earlier.
